review_method: Physical PDF pages rendered with pdftoppm and read alongside complete plain/layout extraction; candidates alone were not used as proof of absence.

parser_bug_items.issue: Source item was token-trimmed before Chinese clause splitting, discarding tokenless continuation sentences.
examples: VTBS NAV fault operational caution, p317/p1166

parser_bug_items.issue: One remaining English sentence was always assigned to the first Chinese clause even when that clause was missing in the English source.
examples: VTBS STAR clause incorrectly received the following pavement/towing English clause, p315/p1163-1164

parser_bug_items.issue: Greedy exact-token skipping could borrow a later source item with a common token; alignment now requires an unambiguous globally monotonic assignment.
Joined annunciation words in extracted Chinese text produced false NAV/GPS token differences, although the rendered Chinese page has the same spaced words as English.
Runway pair ends, reverse runway labels, short taxiway identifiers, attached UTC and explicit bilingual acronym expansions were not extracted consistently.
Wind shear with a space was not recognized as windshear; turbulence remains a non-equivalent concept.
Current-manual source provenance was populated from old static airport page ranges (e.g. ZSPD 448-451 instead of current 584-587). Dynamic chapter page metadata now comes from the actual PDF headers.
Equivalent arrival/approach/landing headings and decimal list numbering without terminal dots needed structural coverage.

source_findings.chinese_exact_clause: 将W19航线MASGU-MABAG-OGABI-NOMAR 航段调整为MASGU- UPMIP-ATKAV-OLPAB-NOMAR供华东方向落地广州航班及飞跃 珠三角航班使用。
source_findings.english_exact_clause: The W19 route segment MASGU-MABAG-OGABI-NOMAR will be adjusted to MASGU-UPMIP-ATKAV-OBLAP-NOMAR for flights landing in Guangzhou and those flying over the Pearl River Delta region bound for East China.
source_findings.evidence: Both pages show Navigation routes item 1 with W19 and the same surrounding MASGU/UPMIP/ATKAV/NOMAR sequence. Rendered glyphs confirm OLPAB versus OBLAP, not a text-extraction substitution.
source_findings.cross_reference_conclusion: The other OBLAP occurrences concern Changzhou/Yangzhou via EMRID/V143/OLRIS; they do not independently confirm this W19 revision. Frequency of spelling is not authority to choose either waypoint. No spelling has been selected or rewritten.

source_findings.chinese_exact_clause: 会指挥速度180到8海里，尽量满足避免造成间隔不够。
source_findings.english_exact_clause: The vessel shall maintain a speed of 180 to 8 knots, ensuring sufficient spacing to avoid insufficient intervals.
source_findings.evidence: Both are Entry / Command Characteristics subitem (2). English does exist and the parser extracts it as arrival sequence 1. It says 8 knots rather than the Chinese distance 8 nautical miles, and describes a speed range rather than retaining a speed to a distance. Pairing cannot repair this source-level unit/meaning conflict; empty pairing is not classified as missing source.

source_findings.chinese_exact_clause: 航图新增Z 进近程序为主用程序，数据库也有变化，提示机组注意阅读对应进场图中Warning 中的说明，避免未经ATC 许可转向五边加入进近程序。
source_findings.english_exact_clause: The new Z approach procedure has been designated as the primary procedure in the air chart, with corresponding database updates. Crews are advised to carefully review the Warning section in the relevant approach chart to prevent unauthorized five-way turns into the approach procedure without ATC clearance.
source_findings.evidence: Corresponding Arrival / Command Characteristics subitem (3) is fully extracted and paired. The rendered English itself says five-way turns, not final approach. This is a source-English semantic-quality difference, not a missing paragraph or page-continuation bug; no generated replacement was supplied.

English Precautions (1) starts at the bottom of p1166 and continues on p1167; the parser retains the full item. English (2) is also present. Rendered English uses 20R RNP five sides and three-way approach, whereas Chinese uses 五边 and 三边航向. Numeric/runway anchors now match, but the existing final-approach semantic guard still rejects the English. This is not a coverage gap; it needs source-English review, not an unreviewed automatic translation.

Chinese item 4.4 says ATC可能指挥短切五边; English item 4.4 says ATC may assign short base-leg vectors. Correct same numbered counterpart is present and paired, and runway/ATC/ILS anchors match after extraction fixes. The final-approach concept guard does not consider base-leg an equivalent final approach. This is documented as a source-language semantic difference requiring authoritative review, not asserted as a proven wrong procedure and not bypassed.
